# Tailwind CSS Engineering Rules

## Configuration & Design Tokens

- All design decisions (colors, spacing, typography, border radius, shadows) must be expressed in `tailwind.config.ts` under `theme.extend`. Do not introduce ad-hoc values via arbitrary `[]` syntax except for genuine one-off exceptions.
- Source design tokens from a single authoritative file (e.g., a design system token JSON or a brand config) and map them into `tailwind.config.ts` programmatically. Do not duplicate token values manually.
- Semantic color tokens (e.g., `color-primary`, `color-surface`, `color-on-error`) must be defined in the theme. Never reference raw palette values (e.g., `bg-blue-500`) directly in component markup.
- Use CSS custom properties (variables) for tokens that change between themes or modes. Reference variables inside `tailwind.config.ts` so utilities remain responsive to runtime token changes.
- Never override the default Tailwind theme outside of `theme.extend`. Replacing the base theme removes the design constraint that makes Tailwind effective.

## Utility Application & Class Authoring

- Apply utility classes directly on elements in JSX/HTML. Do not write custom CSS classes that duplicate what a utility combination achieves.
- Group classes in a consistent order: layout → box model → typography → visual (color, border, shadow) → interactivity → responsive/state variants. Enforce this with `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss`.
- Extract a component abstraction when the same class combination repeats across three or more independent locations. Use `@apply` in a CSS module or a shared React component — not an unstructured utility string copy-pasted across files.
- Use `@apply` sparingly and only in component-level CSS files. Do not use `@apply` to rebuild utility combinations in global stylesheets.
- Avoid string interpolation to build class names at runtime (e.g., `` `bg-${color}-500` ``). Tailwind's JIT compiler performs static analysis; dynamically constructed class strings are not included in the output.

## Responsive Design

- Design mobile-first. Apply base styles without a breakpoint prefix; use `sm:`, `md:`, `lg:`, `xl:` to progressively enhance for larger viewports.
- Use only the breakpoints defined in `tailwind.config.ts`. Do not introduce arbitrary breakpoints via `min-[]` unless no defined breakpoint fits and a design-system exception is documented.
- Avoid breakpoint-driven layout inversions (e.g., hiding on mobile and showing on desktop with a completely different component). Use responsive utilities to adapt a single component rather than duplicating components per breakpoint.

## Dark Mode & Theming

- Set `darkMode: 'class'` in `tailwind.config.ts`. Do not use `'media'` for products that offer a user-controlled theme toggle.
- Apply dark mode variants (`dark:`) only to semantic token utilities. If dark variants are applied directly to palette utilities (e.g., `dark:bg-gray-900`), the token layer is being bypassed.
- Manage theme state (light/dark/system) at the application root. Persist user preference to `localStorage` and apply the `dark` class before first paint to prevent flash.

## Component Abstraction & Scalability

- Create a shared `Button`, `Input`, `Card`, and similar primitive components that encapsulate their Tailwind class sets. Consumers use the component, not raw utility strings, for design-system UI.
- Accept a `className` prop on shared components to allow contextual overrides. Use a class-merging utility (e.g., `clsx` + `tailwind-merge`) to resolve conflicts between base classes and override classes predictably.
- Do not expose internal Tailwind class strings as part of a component's public API (e.g., `baseClassName` props). The component's visual contract is expressed through explicit props, not through class pass-throughs.
- Variant-driven components (size, intent, state) must declare their variants explicitly and use a variant utility (e.g., `cva`) instead of ternary chains of class strings in JSX.

## Performance & Build Output

- Enable JIT mode (default in Tailwind v3+). Do not disable JIT or configure a `safelist` without a documented reason; safelisted classes bypass tree-shaking and inflate bundle size.
- Configure `content` paths in `tailwind.config.ts` precisely. Overly broad globs (e.g., `'**/*'`) slow builds and risk including generated files that produce spurious classes.
- Audit the generated CSS size on every major dependency or design-token change. The compressed Tailwind output for a typical application should remain under 20 kB.
- Do not import Tailwind's full stylesheet in tests or Storybook without a scoped build. Use a test-specific Tailwind config that includes only the content paths relevant to the component under test.

## Accessibility

- Do not use color alone to convey state (focus, error, disabled). Pair color utilities with accessible indicators: `ring`, `border`, `aria-*`, or visible text.
- Apply focus-visible utilities (`focus-visible:ring-*`) to all interactive elements. Do not suppress focus outlines with `outline-none` without providing a visible replacement.
- Use `sr-only` for text that must be present for screen readers but hidden visually. Do not use `hidden` or `invisible` on content that screen readers should read.

## Engineering Standards

- Run `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss` in CI to enforce class ordering. PRs with unsorted utility classes must not be merged.
- Prohibit arbitrary value usage (`[value]`) for any token that can be expressed via the design system. Enforce this with an ESLint rule or a custom `prettier-plugin-tailwindcss` config.
- Document all custom theme extensions with a comment referencing the design system token name or the design decision they encode.
